data.objective: Paint correction before ceramic coating — remove visible paint imperfections and prepare the surface for long-term protection.

data.rootCause: The render has a strong opening and premium polish visuals, but the actual timeline falls apart in the back half: the CTA shot is held far too long, the ending text is oversized and repetitive, and the edit visually stalls instead of closing with a crisp commercial finish. The requested process story is also weakened by using interior/wheel footage as proxy proof, which creates message drift even though the hook itself is solid.

issues.problem: The CTA section is held for multiple seconds on nearly identical frames, which kills momentum and makes the ending feel stuck rather than decisive.
issues.fix: Reduce the final CTA hold to one short hero beat, then cut out or shorten all repeated frames so the reel ends cleanly and punchily.

issues.problem: The reel overextends the final service-context shot instead of ending on the result or a decisive booking moment. This weakens the commercial arc.
issues.fix: Reorder so the final reveal lands closer to the CTA, and shorten the interior shot so it functions as a brief brand context beat only.

issues.problem: The 'Remove imperfections' line is paired with wheel/interior-style footage rather than a true paint defect correction moment, so the visual proof is indirect.
issues.fix: Either reduce reliance on that claim or use the polish/reveal shots to carry the correction message more honestly.

issues.problem: The last four seconds repeat the same interior vacuum shot with the same text, creating dead time and repetition.
issues.fix: Use a single CTA shot, then cut out the duplicates and replace with either the gloss reveal or an earlier process beat if timing is needed.

issues.problem: The CTA text is too large and heavy for the shot, crowding the lower-left corner and feeling more like a caption dump than a polished offer lockup.
issues.fix: Shrink the CTA copy, give it more breathing room, and use a cleaner two-line stack with better safe-area margins.

issues.problem: Brand naming appears only at the end and is not visually integrated throughout the reel.
issues.fix: Keep the ending brand lockup, but consider a lighter early brand cue or logo treatment if available in the same shot set.
